BiblicalUsage: Yâshaṭ means to hold out, to extend. Esther knew the law: whoever came to the king uncalled would die, unless the king held out the golden sceptre that he might live. When the king saw Esther, he held out the sceptre, and she drew near and touched the top of it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sceptre held out is grace, and Esther's courage was to draw near and touch it.
